user_prompt:
In the ΔABC the altitudes BN and CM intersect at point S. The measure of ∠MSB is 40° and the measure of ∠SBC is 20°. Write a PROOF of the following statement:

“ΔABC is isosceles.”

Give geometric reasons for statements in your proof.

[Image: Triangle ABC with altitudes BN and CM intersecting at S]

Figure, described in words:
A triangle ABC with vertex A at the top, vertex B at the bottom left, and vertex C at the bottom right. Segment BN is an altitude drawn from B to AC, with a right-angle symbol at N. Segment CM is an altitude drawn from C to AB, with a right-angle symbol at M. BN and CM intersect at interior point S. The angle MSB is marked with an arc and labeled 40°. The angle SBC is marked with an arc and labeled 20°.

answer.title: Answer

output.answer:
PROOF. Given: BN ⊥ AC (altitude from B, foot N), CM ⊥ AB (altitude from C, foot M), BN and CM meet at S, ∠MSB = 40°, ∠SBC = 20°. Show AB = AC.

Statement 1: ∠CMB = 90° and ∠BNC = 90°. Reason: CM and BN are altitudes, so they are perpendicular to the sides AB and AC respectively.

Statement 2: ∠SMB = 90°. Reason: S lies on segment CM, so ray MS is ray MC, and ∠SMB = ∠CMB = 90°.

Statement 3: ∠MBS = 50°. Reason: In triangle SMB, the angle sum is 180°, so ∠MBS = 180° − ∠MSB − ∠SMB = 180° − 40° − 90° = 50°.

Statement 4: Ray BS = ray BN and ray BM = ray BA. Reason: S lies on segment BN, and M lies on side AB. Therefore ∠ABN = ∠MBS = 50°. (The altitudes meet at the interior point S, so the triangle is acute and the feet M and N lie on the sides.)

Statement 5: ∠NBC = ∠SBC = 20°. Reason: Given, and ray BS = ray BN.

Statement 6: ∠ABC = 70°. Reason: Ray BN lies inside angle ABC, so ∠ABC = ∠ABN + ∠NBC = 50° + 20° = 70°.

Statement 7: ∠BCN = 70°. Reason: In triangle BNC, ∠BNC = 90° and ∠NBC = 20°, so the angle sum gives ∠BCN = 180° − 90° − 20° = 70°.

Statement 8: ∠ACB = 70°. Reason: N lies on side AC, so ray CN = ray CA, and therefore ∠ACB = ∠NCB = 70°.

Statement 9: ∠ABC = ∠ACB = 70°. Reason: From statements 6 and 8.

Statement 10: AB = AC, so ΔABC is isosceles. Reason: A triangle with two equal angles is isosceles (the sides opposite the equal angles are equal, by the converse of the isosceles triangle theorem). Here the sides opposite ∠ACB and ∠ABC are AB and AC. ∎
